## Proof

We are given two Itô integrals driven by the same standard Brownian motion $(B_s)_{s\ge 0}$:

$$X_t = \int_0^t e^s \cos(B_s)\,dB_s, \qquad X_u = \int_0^u e^s \sin(B_s)\,dB_s, \qquad 0\le u\le t.$$

**Step 1 — Both integrals have mean zero.**

The integrands $e^s\cos(B_s)$ and $e^s\sin(B_s)$ are adapted, square-integrable processes (since $|\cos|,|\sin|\le 1$ and $e^s$ is deterministic on $[0,t]$). By the martingale property of the Itô integral,

$$\mathbb{E}[X_t] = \mathbb{E}[X_u] = 0.$$

Hence

$$\operatorname{Cov}(X_t, X_u) = \mathbb{E}[X_t X_u].$$

**Step 2 — Apply the bilinear form of Itô isometry.**

For two Itô integrals driven by the same Brownian motion with adapted, square-integrable integrands $f_s, g_s$,

$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[\int_0^t f_s\,dB_s \cdot \int_0^u g_s\,dB_s\right] = \mathbb{E}\!\left[\int_0^{\min(t,u)} f_s\, g_s\,ds\right].$$

Since $u\le t$, $\min(t,u)=u$, giving

$$\operatorname{Cov}(X_t,X_u) = \mathbb{E}\!\left[\int_0^u e^s\cos(B_s)\cdot e^s\sin(B_s)\,ds\right] = \int_0^u e^{2s}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\cos(B_s)\sin(B_s)\right]ds.$$

**Step 3 — Evaluate $\mathbb{E}[\cos(B_s)\sin(B_s)]$.**

Using the double-angle identity,

$$\cos(B_s)\sin(B_s) = \tfrac{1}{2}\sin(2B_s).$$

Since $B_s\sim\mathcal{N}(0,s)$, its characteristic function is

$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{i\xi B_s}\right] = e^{-\xi^2 s/2}.$$

Taking imaginary parts with $\xi=2$:

$$\mathbb{E}[\sin(2B_s)] = \operatorname{Im}\!\left(\mathbb{E}[e^{i\cdot 2\,B_s}]\right) = \operatorname{Im}\!\left(e^{-2s}\right) = 0,$$

because $e^{-2s}$ is real for $s\ge 0$. Therefore

$$\mathbb{E}[\cos(B_s)\sin(B_s)] = \tfrac{1}{2}\cdot 0 = 0.$$

**Step 4 — Conclude.**

Substituting back,

$$\operatorname{Cov}(X_t, X_u) = \int_0^u e^{2s}\cdot 0\,ds = 0.$$

### Result

$$\boxed{\operatorname{Cov}(X_t, X_u) = 0 \quad \text{for all } 0\le u\le t.}$$

The cross-covariance vanishes identically. Intuitively, $\cos(B_s)$ is an even function of $B_s$ while $\sin(B_s)$ is an odd function of $B_s$; since $B_s$ has a symmetric (centered Gaussian) distribution, the pointwise product $\cos(B_s)\sin(B_s)$ has zero expectation at every $s$, and the Itô isometry propagates this to zero cross-covariance.

### PROOF COMPLETE
